title: Useful General Intelligence — Danielle Perszyk, Amazon AGI
talk_summary: A cognitive-science keynote arguing that general intelligence is social and distributed, so agents should be built to augment humans rather than replace them, illustrated with Amazon's Nova Act browser agent. It is almost entirely vision and philosophy, with only incidental engineering detail about atomic UI actions and parallel browser execution.

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately scope the agent to the smallest reliable unit of interaction (a single act call) and let developers string atomic actions into complex workflows, rather than asking one model call to do a whole workflow.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We are focusing on making the smallest units of interaction reliable and giving you granular control over them.

takeaways.technique: Parallel isolated browser/VM instances per task
takeaways.what_they_do: The demo fans out one browser instance per address using a Python thread pool, then aggregates results, instead of serial execution.
takeaways.evidence_quote: let's do this in parallel. Since this is Python, we can just use a thread pool to spin up multiple browsers, one for each address.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent output is constrained to a Pydantic class and returned as JSON matching that schema, then consumed by ordinary code (pandas).
takeaways.evidence_quote: We'll define a pyantic class and ask the agent to return JSON matching that schema.
